headings.h1: Gauge for radial progress and dial metrics

intro: Gauge turns determinate values into a compact circular visualization. Choose a complete radial ring or an open dial while retaining real meter semantics, explicit ranges, labels, and readable values.
useCases: Dashboard KPIs such as capacity, utilization, and health scores.
Compact completion indicators where a linear bar does not fit.

faqs.question: How is Gauge different from Progress?
faqs.answer: Gauge presents a determinate value as a circular ring or open dial and uses meter semantics. Progress remains the linear progress-bar primitive for task completion.

faqs.question: Can Gauge use a custom range and value format?
faqs.answer: Yes. Set min and max for the range and use formatValue to render units, scores, storage values, or another readable string. The same text is exposed to assistive technology.

faqs.question: Is the Gauge component accessible?
faqs.answer: The root uses role='meter' with minimum, maximum, current, and textual values. Supply a concise label that describes the measured quantity.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: Gauge maps a value within a configurable range onto an SVG arc. Values outside that range are clamped so the graphic and accessible meter state remain aligned.

sections.heading: Radial and dial variants
sections.body: Use the default radial variant for a complete 360-degree ring. Choose the dial variant for a rounded 270-degree arc with an open lower edge, which reads naturally for performance and capacity metrics.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.body: The visible percentage is not the only source of meaning. Gauge exposes meter semantics, the numeric range, current value, a readable value string, and an accessible label on the root.

sections.heading: Next.js integration notes
sections.body: Gauge is exported from its own client entry and has no Framer Motion dependency. Import it from @zentauri-ui/zentauri-components/ui/gauge in an App Router client subtree or render it through a server component boundary.
